title: 집 · 거주지
intro: OPIc 설문에서 거의 항상 출제되는 핵심 주제로, 집 묘사 → 집에서의 일상 → 집과 관련된 경험(고장·문제) → 예전 집과 비교 순서로 나옵니다. 모든 답변은 '서울에서 가족(엄마, 아빠, 남동생 Junho)과 사는 10층 아파트, 방 3개, 작은 발코니, 10년째 거주'라는 하나의 집으로 통일하세요. 자기소개에서 말한 '가족과 서울에 산다'가 그대로 이어집니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Okay, let me tell you about my home.' → 기본 정보(아파트, 10층, 가족과, 10년째) → 공간 소개(거실·부엌·내 방) → 제일 좋아하는 공간과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's my home.' 마무리
묘사는 '들어가면 → 왼쪽/오른쪽 → 내 방' 순서처럼 길을 안내하듯 말하면 문장이 끊기지 않습니다.
경험 질문은 언제 → 무슨 일 → 어떻게 해결 → 느낀 점을 과거시제로 말하고, 'Yeah, that was ~'로 끝냅니다.
IH 이상은 비교(compared to, used to)와 감정·소리·빛 같은 생생한 디테일을 추가합니다.

expressions.en: Okay, let me tell you about my home.
I live in an apartment in Seoul with my family.
expressions.ko: 저는 서울에 있는 아파트에서 가족과 함께 살아요.

expressions.en: Our apartment is on the 10th floor.
It has three bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and a small balcony.
expressions.ko: 방 세 개, 거실, 부엌, 작은 발코니가 있어요.

expressions.en: We've been living here for about ten years.
When you walk in, the first thing you see is the living room.
expressions.ko: 들어가면 제일 먼저 보이는 게 거실이에요.

expressions.en: In my room, there's a bed, a desk, and a small bookshelf.
expressions.ko: 제 방에는 침대, 책상, 작은 책장이 있어요.

expressions.en: My favorite place in my home is my room because it's quiet and cozy.
expressions.ko: 집에서 제일 좋아하는 곳은 제 방이에요. 조용하고 아늑하거든요.

expressions.en: What I like most about our place is that the subway station is only five minutes away.
expressions.ko: 우리 집에서 제일 좋은 건 지하철역이 5분 거리라는 거예요.
expressions.note: What I like most about ~ is that ~

expressions.en: Compared to our old place, this one is much bigger and brighter.
expressions.ko: 예전 집에 비하면 여기가 훨씬 넓고 밝아요.

expressions.en: I used to share a room with my younger brother.
The boiler suddenly stopped working in the middle of winter.
So yeah, that's pretty much what my home is like.
It's nothing fancy, but it's where I feel the most like myself.
expressions.ko: 화려하진 않지만, 제가 가장 저다워지는 곳이에요.

expressions.en: After living here for ten years, every corner of this place has a memory attached to it.
expressions.ko: 여기서 10년을 살다 보니 구석구석마다 추억이 담겨 있어요.
expressions.note: have a memory attached to it

questions.en: I'd like to know about where you live. Can you describe your home? What does it look like, and how many rooms does it have?
questions.ko: 어디에 사는지 알고 싶어요. 집을 묘사해 주시겠어요? 어떻게 생겼고, 방은 몇 개인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 아파트·층·가족·거주 기간 → 거실·부엌·내 방 → 제일 좋아하는 공간과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'When you walk in, the first thing you see is ~'로 길 안내하듯 묘사하세요.
IH 이상은 창밖 풍경, 햇빛, 소리 같은 감각 디테일을 하나 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my home. I live in an apartment in Seoul with my family. It's on the 10th floor. We've been living here for about ten years. It has three bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and a small balcony. The living room is pretty big, and we have a big TV there. In my room, there's a bed, a desk, a laptop, and a small bookshelf. My room is my favorite place because it's quiet and cozy. Yeah, that's my home.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about my home. I live in an apartment in Seoul with my mom, my dad, and my younger brother Junho. It's on the 10th floor, and we've been living here for about ten years. It has three bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and a small balcony. When you walk in, the first thing you see is the living room. It has a big sofa and a TV, and that's where my family watches movies together on weekends. The kitchen is right next to it, so the space feels open. My room is at the end of the hallway. There's a bed, a desk with my laptop, and a small bookshelf. It's not very big, but it's really cozy. What I like most about our place is that the subway station is only five minutes away. So yeah, that's pretty much what my home is like.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about my home. I live in an apartment in Seoul with my family, which is my mom, my dad, and my younger brother Junho. We're on the 10th floor, and we've been living here for about ten years, so it really feels like our place. It has three bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and a small balcony. As soon as you walk in, you see the living room, which is kind of the heart of our home. There's a big comfy sofa and a TV, and on weekend nights, the four of us usually end up there watching a movie together. The kitchen is right next to the living room, so you can smell whatever my mom is cooking from anywhere in the house. My room is at the end of the hallway. It's not huge, but it has everything I need, like a bed, a desk with my laptop, and a small bookshelf full of old books and photos. In the afternoon, the sun comes in through my window, and it's honestly the coziest spot in the whole apartment. It's nothing fancy, but it's where I feel the most like myself. Yeah, that's pretty much my home.

questions.en: What do you usually do at home? Tell me about a typical day at your home from morning to night.
questions.ko: 집에서 보통 무엇을 하나요? 아침부터 밤까지 집에서의 하루를 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Sure, I'd love to talk about that.' → 아침(준비·아침 식사) → 저녁(가족과 식사) → 밤(과제·영화) → 주말 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
평일과 주말을 나눠 말하면 자연스럽게 길이가 늘어납니다.
'I usually ~', 'After that, ~', 'On weekends, ~'처럼 빈도·순서 표현을 쓰세요.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. On weekdays, I'm not home much because I have a lot of classes. In the morning, I get ready and have breakfast with my family. I come home around seven in the evening. Then we have dinner together in the kitchen. After dinner, I do my homework at my desk. Before bed, I watch Netflix on my laptop. On weekends, I sleep in and relax at home. Yeah, that's what I usually do at home.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. On weekdays, I don't spend much time at home because I usually have a lot of classes. In the morning, I get up at seven, take a quick shower, and have breakfast with my family in the kitchen. Then I leave for school around eight. I usually get home around seven in the evening, and we have dinner together. My mom is a great cook, so dinner is my favorite part of the day. After dinner, I go to my room and do my assignments on my laptop. When I'm done, I listen to music or watch a short video in bed. Weekends are totally different. I sleep in until ten, clean my room a little, and then just relax. On Saturday nights, my family watches a movie together in the living room. Yeah, that's pretty much my day at home.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. To be honest, on weekdays I'm barely home, because my schedule is packed with classes. My mornings are pretty rushed. I get up at seven, jump in the shower, and grab some breakfast with my family before heading out around eight. The real home time starts when I get back around seven in the evening. We almost always have dinner together, and it's kind of our time to catch up. My dad talks about work, Junho complains about school, and my mom makes sure we all eat enough. After dinner, I go to my room, sit at my desk, and work on my assignments on my laptop. Once I'm done, I usually lie in bed with my earphones in, listening to some ballads or watching a short video. Weekends are a whole different story. I sleep in until about ten, which feels amazing after a long week. I spend the afternoon tidying up my room or just lying around on the sofa. Then on Saturday nights, the four of us pick a movie and watch it together in the living room with some snacks. It's nothing special, but that's the part of the week I look forward to the most. Yeah, that's what my days at home look like.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem at your home, like something breaking? Tell me what happened and how you handled it.
questions.ko: 집에서 뭔가 고장 나는 등 문제가 생긴 적이 있나요? 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 해결했는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a problem at home? Let me think.' → 언제·무슨 문제 → 그때 상황·느낌 → 해결 과정 → 결과와 배운 점 → 'Yeah, that was ~' 마무리
과거시제를 일관되게 쓰고, 'suddenly', 'luckily', 'in the end'로 이야기를 연결하세요.
IH 이상은 그때의 감정(cold, nervous, relieved)을 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Last winter, our boiler broke. It was a very cold night in January. We didn't have any hot water, and the house was really cold. My dad called a repairman, but he couldn't come until the next day. So we wore thick sweaters and used extra blankets. The next morning, the repairman fixed the boiler. It took about one hour. I was so happy. Yeah, that was a pretty cold night.
answers.IH: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Last winter, our boiler suddenly stopped working. It was a really cold night in January, and I was studying for my final exams in my room. All of a sudden, the floor got cold, and there was no hot water. My dad called the repair service right away, but they said they couldn't come until the next morning. So my family put on thick sweaters and used extra blankets. My brother Junho and I even slept in the living room with our parents to stay warm. It was kind of funny, like camping at home. The next morning, a repairman came and fixed it in about an hour. After that, my dad started checking the boiler every fall. Yeah, that was a cold but pretty memorable night.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Actually, something happened last winter that I'll never forget. It was a freezing night in January, right in the middle of my final exams. I was sitting at my desk studying, and I slowly realized my feet were getting cold. At first, I thought it was just me, but then my mom shouted from the bathroom that there was no hot water. Our boiler had completely stopped working. My dad called the repair service right away, but since it was so late, nobody could come until the next morning. So we had to get creative. We all put on thick sweaters, pulled out every blanket we had, and the four of us ended up sleeping on the living room floor together. Junho kept joking that it felt like a family camping trip, and honestly, it kind of did. The next morning, a repairman came and fixed it in about an hour. It turned out one small part had worn out after years of use. Looking back, it was a stressful night, especially with my exams, but it's also one of the funniest memories I have with my family. Since then, my dad checks the boiler every fall. Yeah, that was a cold night I'll always remember.

questions.en: How is the home you live in now different from the home you lived in when you were a child?
questions.ko: 지금 사는 집은 어렸을 때 살던 집과 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, my old home? Let me think.' → 예전 집 소개 → 지금 집과 다른 점 2~3개 → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
지금 집에 10년째 산다는 설정과 맞춰, 이사 온 시기를 '초등학생 때, 10년 전쯤'으로 통일하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, my old home? Let me think. When I was a child, we lived in a small apartment in a different part of Seoul. It had only two bedrooms, so I shared a room with my brother Junho. About ten years ago, we moved to our current apartment. It's much bigger and brighter. It has three bedrooms, so now I have my own room. It's also close to a subway station. I like my home now much better. Yeah, that's the difference.
answers.IH: Oh, my old home? Let me think. When I was in elementary school, my family lived in a small, old apartment in a different part of Seoul. It was on the second floor, and it only had two bedrooms. So I used to share a room with my younger brother Junho, and we fought all the time. About ten years ago, we moved to our current apartment. Compared to our old place, this one is much bigger and brighter. It has three bedrooms, so I finally got my own room. It's on the 10th floor, so we get a lot of sunlight, and we even have a small balcony. Also, the subway station is only five minutes away, which is great for me as a college student. I do miss the old place a little, but I like my home now much better. Yeah, that's the biggest difference.
answers.AL: Oh, my old home? Let me think. When I was little, my family lived in a small, old apartment in a different part of Seoul. It was on the second floor and only had two bedrooms, so my younger brother Junho and I had to share a room. Back then, we fought over everything, like who got the bigger side of the desk or when to turn off the lights. The place was also pretty dark, because there was another building right in front of our windows. About ten years ago, when I was in elementary school, we moved to the apartment we live in now, and it was a huge change. Compared to the old place, it's much bigger and so much brighter. We're on the 10th floor, so the sun pours in, and we even have a small balcony where my mom grows plants. Best of all, I finally got my own room, which felt like a dream at the time. The location is a lot more convenient too, since the subway station is just five minutes away. To be honest, I still miss the old place sometimes, because that's where I spent my early childhood. But if I had to choose, I'd definitely pick where I live now. Yeah, that's pretty much how they're different.
